May, 2024
Author: Anil Kumar Choudhary

Bench: Anil Kumar Choudhary
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
 Cr.M.P. No. 2688 of 2022
 Binay Tiwary @ Vinay Tiwary, aged about 34 years, son of
 Chandeshwar Tiwary @ Chandrashekar Tiwary, resident of Quarter
 No. 209, New Baridih, Panchwati Road, P.O. -Baridih, P.S. -Sidgoda,
 Jamshedpur, District -East Singhbhum.

By the Court:-
 1. Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding including the F.I.R. of Bistupur P.S. Case No. 55 of 2022, registered for the offences punishable under Section 323/506/406/420 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner who is a relative of the complainant took a friendly loan of Rs.25,00,000/- from Binay Tiwary @ Vinay Tiwary vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49471849/
1

entities.text: Binay Tiwary @ Vinay Tiwary vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the complainant through bank transactions and an agreement was entered into between the parties that the petitioner will return the friendly loan of Rs.25,00,000/- within three months but the same was not returned within three months and when the informant demanded the money, the petitioner issued a cheque of Rs.25,00,000/- in the name of his business firm Vinod Tiwary Roadways.
The informant presented the cheque in her account for encashment but the same was dishonoured as there was no money in the account.
After that, the informant demanded the money from the petitioner but the petitioner assured that he will return the money.
On 17.12.2020, through her Advocate, the informant sent a legal notice demanding money which was duly received by the petitioner but the same was not replied to by the petitioner.

Alleging that as a pre-planned conspiracy, the petitioner has committed cheating and has induced the informant to pay Rs.25,00,000/-, the informant instituted Complaint Case No. 781 of 2021 in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamshedpur.

The said case was referred to police under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. and on the basis of the same, Bistupur P.S. Case No. 55 of 2022 has been registered.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the informant has filed this case suppressing the material fact that for the dishonour of the cheque, earlier the informant -complainant filed Complaint Case No. 164 of 2021 in which the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Jamshedpur has found prima facie case for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the N.I. Act and issued summons to the petitioner and the petitioner is on bail in that case as is evident from the order sheet dated 24.02.2022.
It is next submitted that there is abnormal delay in institution of the complaint and this is the second complaint in respect of the selfsame allegations which is not maintainable.

It is then submitted that even if the allegations are considered to be true in their entirety, still the offence punishable under Section 420 or 406 of the Indian Penal Code is not made out and there is no allegation of any criminal intimidation or causing hurt to the informant or anybody else.

5. Relying upon the Judgment of this Court in the case of Ajay Sagar @ Ajay Prem Sagar & Ors. Vs.
The State of Jharkhand & Anr., in Cr.M.P. No. 3781 of 2022 dated 28.06.2023, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that this Court in the aforesaid case relied upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in the case of Krishna Lal Chawla & Others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Another, reported in (2021) 5 SCC 435, para -13 & 26 of which reads as under:-
13.

Ajay Sagar @ Ajay Prem Sagar & Ors. Vs.
The State of Jharkhand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Krishna Lal Chawla & Others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Another, reported in (2021) 5 SCC 435
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also crucial to note that in the fresh complaint case instituted by him,
Respondent 2 seems to have deliberately suppressed the material fact that a charge-sheet was already filed in relation to the same incident, against him and his wife, pursuant to NCR No. 160 of 2012 (Crime No. 283 of 2017) filed by Appellant 1's son.
No reference to this charge-sheet is found in the private complaint, or in the statements under Section 200 CrPC filed by Respondent 2 and his wife.

In fact, both the private complaint and the statement filed on behalf of his wife, merely state that the police officials have informed them that investigation is ongoing pursuant to their NCR No. 158 of 2012.
The wife's statement additionally even states that no action has been taken so far by the police.
It is the litigant's bounden duty to make a full and true disclosure of facts.

It is a matter of trite law, and yet bears repetition, that suppression of material facts before a court amounts to abuse of the Binay Tiwary @ Vinay Tiwary vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49471849/
2 process of the court, and shall be dealt with a heavy hand (Ram Dhan v. State of U.P. [Ram Dhan v.
State of U.P., (2012) 5 SCC 536 : (2012) 3 SCC (Cri) 237] ; K.D. Sharma v. SAIL [K.D. Sharma v.
SAIL, (2008) 12 SCC 481] ).
26.

Ram Dhan v. State of U.P. [Ram Dhan v.
State of U.P., (2012) 5 SCC 536 : (2012) 3 SCC (Cri) 237]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
K.D. Sharma v. SAIL [K.D. Sharma v.
SAIL, (2008) 12 SCC 481]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a settled canon of law that this Court has inherent powers to prevent the abuse of its own processes, that this Court shall not suffer a litigant utilising the institution of justice for unjust means.
Thus, it would be only proper for this Court to deny any relief to a litigant who attempts to pollute the stream of justice by coming to it with his unclean hands.
Similarly, a litigant pursuing frivolous and vexatious proceedings cannot claim unlimited right upon court time and public money to achieve his ends."
(Emphasis supplied)

And considered that since it is the litigant's bounden duty to make a full and true disclosure of facts and it is a matter of trite law that suppression of material facts before a court amounts to abuse of the process of the court, hence the same shall be dealt with a heavy hand.
It is therefore, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that on this score alone, the entire criminal proceeding against the petitioner is liable to be quashed and set aside.

6. It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that in the case of Ajay Sagar @
Ajay Prem Sagar & Ors. Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Anr. (supra), this Court also relied upon the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Kapil Agarwal & Others Vs. Sanjay Sharma & Others, reported in (2021) 5 SCC 524, para -20 & 21 of which reads as under:-
"20.

entities.text:
Ajay Sagar @
Ajay Prem Sagar & Ors. Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kapil Agarwal & Others Vs. Sanjay Sharma & Others, reported in (2021) 5 SCC 524
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, the impugned FIR is nothing but an abuse of process of law and can be said to be filed with a view to harass the appellants.

21. We are not expressing anything on merits whether, any case is made out against the appellants for the offences alleged in the Section 156(3) CrPC application as the same is pending before the learned Magistrate and the learned Magistrate is to take call on the same.

Therefore, when the impugned FIR is nothing but an abuse of process of law and to harass the appellant-accused, we are of the opinion that the High Court ought to have exercised the powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India/Section 482 CrPC and ought to have quashed the impugned FIR to secure the ends of justice."

And submits that in that case, this Court considered that where the complainant first filed an application under Section 138 of the N.I. Act and subsequently filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. seeking registration of the F.I.R. and subsequently filed another F.I.R. suppressing the fact of earlier order, the subsequent F.I.R. is nothing but an abuse of process of law.

Hence, it is submitted that the entire criminal proceeding including the F.I.R. of Bistupur P.S. Case No. 55 of 2022, registered for the offences punishable under Section 323/506/406/420 of the Indian Penal Code be quashed and set aside.
7. The learned Addl. P.P. submits that there is allegation of abusing and threatening against the petitioner as mentioned in para-8 & 11 of the F.I.R.
Hence, the same is sufficient to constitute the offence punishable under Section 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
Therefore, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that it is a settled principle of law Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Upkar Singh v. Ved Prakash and others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 292,
paragraph no. 17 of which reads and under :-
"17.

entities.text: Upkar Singh v. Ved Prakash and others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 292
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is clear from the words emphasised hereinabove in the above quotation, this Court in the case of T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala [(2001) 6 SCC 181 : 2001 SCC (Cri)
1048] has not excluded the registration of a complaint in the nature of a counter-case from the purview of the Code.

entities.text:
T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala [(2001) 6 SCC 181 : 2001 SCC (Cri)
1048]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In our opinion, this Court in that case only held that any further complaint by the same complainant or others against the same accused,
subsequent to the registration of a case, is prohibited under the Code because an investigation in this regard would have already started and further complaint against the same accused will amount to an improvement on the facts mentioned in the original complaint, hence will be prohibited under Section 162 of the Code.
This prohibition noticed by this Court, in our opinion, does not apply to counter-complaint by the accused in the first complaint or on his behalf alleging a different version of the said incident."

(Emphasis supplied) Thus the law is well settled that any further complaint by the same complainant or others against the same accused, subsequent to the registration of a case, is prohibited under the Code Of Criminal Procedure.

9. Now coming to the facts of the case, after going through the averments made in the complaint of Complaint Case No. 164 of 2021 and 781 of 2021, on the basis of which this Bistupur P.S. Case No.
55 of 2022 has been registered, this Court finds that para-1 to 10 of both the complaints are word by word same and there is a little modification of para -11 & 12 of the complaint of Complaint Case No.
164 of 2021 in para -11 to 14 of this F.I.R. but no new discovery is made on factual foundation of the case in this F.I.R.

entities.text: Complaint Case No. 164 of 2021 and 781 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the continuation of Bisutpur P.S.
Case No. 55 of 2022 which is based on the Complaint Case No. 781 of 2021 amounts to abuse of process of the Court as the same has been filed suppressing the material facts of the same verbatim of para-1 to 10, as the earlier complaint being Complaint Case No. 164 of 2021 which is still pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Jamshedpur.

Hence, in view of the settled principle of law as referred to above in the foregoing paragraphs of the Judgment, this Court is of the considered view that this is a fit case where the entire criminal proceeding including the F.I.R. of Bistupur P.S. Case No. 55 of 2022, registered for the offences punishable under Section 323/506/406/420 of the Indian Penal Code be quashed and set aside.

10. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceeding including the F.I.R.
of Bistupur P.S. Case No. 55 of 2022, registered for the offences punishable under Section 323/506/406/420 of the Indian Penal Code is quashed and set aside.
11. In the result, this criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed.
